boundaries.result: ParticleSystem is borrowed per call; no cached service survives Game/World destruction order.
All callers already pass CameraProjectionSettings. The unused Game overload was the remaining direct Game header dependency in the camera directory.

Structural edits recover file/runtime through transactions. Immediate inspector values remain visible on failure, failed saves keep callbacks, and history is appended only after persistence succeeds. No second transaction framework added.
Sequence/camera/scene/editor references are cleared before replacement; failed load restores old World ownership. Scene spans are synchronous and must not be cached across updates.

Player respawn clears buffered attack, hover, facing target, grounding/gravity and particle history. Enemy resolves pursuit each update and branches on life state. Existing native death/combat/reload regressions retained; this is not proof of every AI path.
UGC grid direction buttons now join other one-shot histories during capture suppression. Static call-site review; no new end-to-end D-pad capture regression is claimed.
WriteActorState already rejects null. WriteTextureState now takes const Actor& instead of a nullable pointer; analyzer warning resolved without suppressing the checker.

boundaries.area: Stable switch target identity and persistence
boundaries.result: ID-only targets are parsed, compared by stable identity, resolved and preserved when saving. Different IDs do not collide on an absent legacy index; owner and duplicate references are filtered. Legacy sequence/index references remain supported.

not_changed: Game composition remains responsible for assembling services. Actors that orchestrate multiple systems keep Game rather than introducing broad provider interfaces.
Mode-specific input histories remain independent booleans; no evidence justified a larger state-machine rewrite.
UGC sample data with unknown intended switch connections remains unchanged and explicitly baselined by content hash.
